# Rust

`transition_matrix!` is a `macro_rules!` macro. No proc-macro crate, no build
script, no dependencies at all -- the library's `[dependencies]` table is
empty, and it builds `#![no_std]` with `default-features = false`. MSRV 1.75.

Not on crates.io yet. Until then, depend on the repository:

```toml
[dependencies]
tabular-center = { git = "https://github.com/tabula-center/tabular-center" }
```

## The matrix

Examples keep the matrix in a file of its own, named `*.tb.rs`
([why](matrix-files)):

```rust
transition_matrix! {
    machine Timer;
    context Ctx;
    state   State;
    action  Action;
    effects Effect { StartClock, StopClock { reason: Reason } }
    initial Idle;

    states  { Idle, Running { since: u64 }, Done }
    actions { Start, Tick { now: u64 }, Cancel }

    //            Start                                  Tick     Cancel
    Idle    => [  HANDLE,                                IGNORE,  IGNORE                                  ];
    Running => [  IGNORE,                                HANDLE,  GO!(Idle, StopClock { reason: Reason::Cancelled }) ];
    Done    => [  GO!(Running { since: 0 }, StartClock), IGNORE,  IGNORE                                  ];
}
```

<sub>From [`tabular-center-rust/examples/02-timer/src/machine.tb.rs`](https://github.com/tabula-center/tabular-center/blob/main/tabular-center-rust/examples/02-timer/src/machine.tb.rs).</sub>

The header names the generated types: `State` and `Action` are enums of the
listed variants, and every variant is also a struct of its own -- `Idle`,
`Running { since }`, `Tick { now }` -- which is what lets a cell receive
exactly its state and action. `effects` declares the effect enum the same way. Each row is a state, each column an action, and each cell one of
six kinds ([Cells](cells)):

| | |
|---|---|
| `HANDLE` | you implement it |
| `IGNORE` | the action means nothing in this state |
| `GO!(Target, Effect...)` | a static transition, emitting effects |
| `EMIT(Effect...)` | stay, emitting effects |
| `DELEGATE!(child)` | hand the cell to a child machine |
| `UNREACHABLE` | a trap, counted by `Table::coverage` |

## The code you write

One `Handle` impl per `HANDLE` cell and one `Perform` impl per effect. Each is
narrowed: the dispatcher has already matched, so `s.since` and `a.now` are
plain fields.

```rust
impl Handle<Timer, Idle, Start> for Impl {
    fn handle(&mut self, _c: &mut Ctx, _s: Idle, _a: Start) -> Step<State, Effect> {
        Step::go(State::Running(Running { since: 0 })).emit(StartClock.into())
    }
}

impl Handle<Timer, Running, Tick> for Impl {
    fn handle(&mut self, c: &mut Ctx, s: Running, a: Tick) -> Step<State, Effect> {
        // No `if let`, no cast, no unwrap: the dispatcher already matched.
        if a.now.saturating_sub(s.since) >= c.limit {
            Step::go(State::Done(Done)).emit(
                StopClock {
                    reason: Reason::Elapsed,
                }
                .into(),
            )
        } else {
            // Handled, and staying put. Distinct from `Ignored`, which would
            // claim a tick is meaningless while running.
            Step::stay()
        }
    }
}

impl Perform<Timer, StartClock> for Impl {
    fn perform(&mut self, c: &mut Ctx, _e: StartClock) -> Option<Action> {
        c.log.push("start".into());
        None
    }
}

impl Perform<Timer, StopClock> for Impl {
    fn perform(&mut self, c: &mut Ctx, e: StopClock) -> Option<Action> {
        c.log.push(format!("stop:{:?}", e.reason));
        None
    }
}
```

<sub>From [`tabular-center-rust/examples/02-timer/src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/tabula-center/tabular-center/blob/main/tabular-center-rust/examples/02-timer/src/lib.rs).</sub>

That is the entire implementation. `step(&mut Impl, &mut ctx, state, action)`
dispatches; `Driver` runs a mailbox over it, so an effect handler that returns
a follow-up action queues it instead of re-entering `step`.

## When a cell is missing

Delete the `Handle<Timer, Running, Tick>` impl and the build stops:

```text
error: the trait bound `T: tabular_center::Handle<Timer, Running, Tick>` is not satisfied
```

That is rustc's own message -- the `step` it generated carries one trait bound
per `HANDLE` cell -- so it names the exact hole and survives even if the
macro is bypassed. It is a fixture: `compile-fail` requires it on every run,
along with one fixture per diagnostic the macro itself emits
([Diagnostics](diagnostics)), such as a row with too few cells.

## Composition

`DELEGATE!(auth)` hands cells to a child machine. The parent's state carries
the child's, and one type implements both:

```rust
transition_matrix! {
    machine Session;
    context Ctx;
    state   State;
    action  Action;
    effects Effect { Audit, Warn, Redirect }
    initial LoggedOut;

    states  { LoggedOut { auth: super::auth::State }, Active, Banned }
    actions { Credentials { ok: u32 }, StartOver, Logout }

    //                 Credentials         StartOver           Logout
    LoggedOut  => [     DELEGATE!(auth),   DELEGATE!(auth),    IGNORE                    ];
    Active     => [     IGNORE,            IGNORE,             GO!(Banned, Audit)        ];
    Banned     => [     IGNORE,            IGNORE,             IGNORE                    ];
}
```

<sub>From [`tabular-center-rust/examples/04-login/src/session.tb.rs`](https://github.com/tabula-center/tabular-center/blob/main/tabular-center-rust/examples/04-login/src/session.tb.rs).</sub>

## Colors

`prototype async fn handle;` after `context` makes the machine async: `step`
becomes an `async fn`, and the cells implement `AsyncHandle` / `AsyncPerform`.
A plain child composes into an async parent; an async child under a plain
parent is refused by rustc.

## Introspection

Every machine has a `TABLE` const describing its matrix, from which the
library renders a diffable grid, Mermaid and DOT diagrams, a coverage report,
and lints -- a column nothing handles, a field repeated across every state that
belongs in the context, a machine that is mostly `IGNORE` (the order lifecycle
on the [front page](./) trips that one, fairly). `table-diff` prints the grid:
`nix run .#table-diff -- timer`.

## Examples

In [`tabular-center-rust/examples`](https://github.com/tabula-center/tabular-center/blob/main/tabular-center-rust/examples), each its own crate:

| | | adds |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `traffic-light` | the minimum; `#![no_std]`, `default-features = false` |
| 2 | `timer` | payloads, effects, narrowed handlers -- the machine above |
| 3 | `retry` | a binary: effects feeding actions back through the driver |
| 4 | `login` | composition, parent and child |
| 5 | `iced` | a GUI: the same machine driving iced, which knows nothing about it |
